mergeResult.summary: {"merged_summary":{"title":"Mapping Your Dollars-to-BS Ratio for Optimal Role Selection","overview":"This synthesis combines insights from two branches focused on designing a practical metric—the Dollars-to-BS (DTB) Ratio—to evaluate job roles or projects based on compensation and workplace friction. The goal is to help individuals identify high-reward, low-friction opportunities, particularly when considering governance-heavy or complex roles, and even geographic moves such as relocating to South Africa.","key_insights":[{"concept":"Dollars-to-BS Ratio (DTB Score)","details":"A metric designed to quantify the trade-off between compensation and workplace friction. It helps prioritize roles or projects that maximize reward while minimizing energy-draining factors."},{"components":{"Compensation ($)":"Total compensation that matters to you, including base salary, bonuses, and valued benefits.","Friction (BS)":"The energy drain caused by fuzziness, politics, low agency, endless meetings, unclear acceptance criteria, and other governance overhead."}},{"formula":"DTB Score = Adjusted Compensation / Friction Hours","adjusted_compensation":"Adjusted Compensation = Annual Compensation × Joy Factor (0.5 to 1.2). Joy Factor reflects how energizing or conflicting the work is to your values (1.2 if energizing, 0.5 if conflicting).","friction_hours":"Friction Hours = Weekly time lost to governance grind × 52 (weeks)."},{"application":"Use the DTB Score to compare roles, projects, or clients. Higher scores indicate better balance of reward to friction.","flexibility":"Can be applied at different granularities—per job, project, or client."},{"practical_tool":"A worksheet or spreadsheet can be created to input compensation, joy factor, and friction hours for each option to calculate and compare DTB Scores."},{"contextual insight from South Africa move branch":"When considering significant changes like relocating to South Africa, this metric helps weigh the financial benefits against potential increases in friction due to new governance, cultural, or operational challenges."}],"recommendations":["Adopt the DTB Score framework to systematically evaluate job or project options.","Customize the Joy Factor based on personal values and energy levels to reflect subjective experience accurately.","Track and estimate friction hours realistically, including governance and political overhead.","Use the metric to inform decisions about geographic moves or role changes, ensuring that compensation gains are not offset by excessive friction.","Develop or use a simple worksheet or digital tool to facilitate ongoing comparisons."],"conflicts_resolved":"No conflicting ideas were present between the branches; rather, the second branch expanded on the first by providing a detailed formula, practical worksheet guidance, and contextual application to relocation decisions.","next_steps":["Create a user-friendly digital calculator or app to automate DTB Score calculations.","Explore case studies applying the DTB Score in various industries and geographies.","Investigate how to quantify and reduce friction factors effectively to improve DTB Scores.","Examine the impact of cultural and governance differences on friction when considering international moves."]}}
